Make the Kaizen kickoff
clear, human and memorable.

The updated slide has useful information, but it is dense and full of internal language. Today you will learn how to turn it into a story an American audience can follow: who you are, why the project matters, what the target is, where the team will act and how questions can be handled.

01 · TRAINER REVIEW

The current slide is useful, but not audience-friendly yet.

It contains the project facts, but a mixed U.S. audience may not immediately understand why the project matters because the slide starts with internal structure and acronyms.

La diapositive contient les faits du projet, mais un public américain non spécialiste risque de se perdre dans les acronymes avant de comprendre l'enjeu.

What may happen with an American audience

  • Too many acronyms too early: NNC, P90, PNR, CSC, CFM56, LEAP, DMAIC may slow comprehension.
  • The human story is missing: the audience does not first hear who you are or why the team was created.
  • The key message is hidden: 12 days today versus 2 days target is the hook, but it is not visually dominant.
  • The team list is too detailed for the main story: useful for credibility, but not what the audience needs first.
  • The slide needs a route: problem → target → impact → scope → plan → questions.
✓

A better strategy

Keep the technical credibility, but move the first 60 seconds into a story: “I’m here with a cross-functional team because non-conformity treatment is taking too long, and our mission is to reduce the lead time from 12 days to 2 days.”

Conservez la crédibilité technique, mais commencez par une histoire claire et humaine.

03 · OPEN WITH A HUMAN STORY

Start with who you are, then move into the project.

For a U.S. audience, a short personal and team introduction can make the technical project easier to connect with.

Pour un public américain, une courte introduction personnelle et équipe aide à rendre le projet plus accessible.

Build your opening one decision at a time

1 · Greeting
2 · Role
3 · Hook
4 · Route
5 · Invite
Supported model · B1

“Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here. I’m leading this Kaizen project with a cross-functional team. The simple story is this: today, the P90 lead time for non-conformity treatment is 12 days, and the target is 2 days. I’ll explain the problem, the target, the impact, the scope and the roadmap. Please stop me if you want me to clarify an acronym or a figure.”

Stronger model · B1+/B2

“Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining this kickoff. My role today is to make the project story clear, not just to walk through technical details. We have a cross-functional team working on one practical challenge: reducing non-conformity treatment lead time from a 12-day P90 today to a 2-day target. I’ll explain why that matters, where we will focus, and how the DMAIC roadmap will help us control the improvement.”

04 · ACRONYM DETOX + USEFUL VOCABULARY

Keep the technical terms, but translate them into meaning.

The audience can accept acronyms if you define them once and then return to plain English.

🧾

NNC

non-conformité

Use once as: “non-conformity treatment, or NNC.”

“To keep it simple, NNC means non-conformity treatment.”

📊

P90 lead time

délai P90

The lead-time level that captures the slower end of the process.

“P90 gives us a realistic view of the slowest cases, not just the average.”

🧭

DMAIC

Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control

The improvement roadmap used to structure the project.

“DMAIC gives us the roadmap: define, measure, analyze, improve and control.”

⚙️

CFM56 & LEAP

programmes moteurs

Engine programmes included in the scope.

“The scope focuses on turbine nozzles and blades for CFM56 and LEAP.”

🎯

the core challenge

le défi principal

The main problem the project addresses.

“The core challenge is to reduce lead time without losing control.”

🚚

on-time delivery

livraison à l'heure

Delivering parts when they are expected.

“The current lead time can put on-time delivery at risk.”

📉

reduce lead time

réduire le délai

Make the process faster from start to finish.

“Our target is to reduce the P90 lead time from 12 days to 2 days.”

🧱

sustainable improvement

amélioration durable

An improvement that can be maintained over time.

“The objective is sustainable improvement, not a temporary drop.”

▶

kick off

lancer

Start the meeting or project phase.

“If everyone’s ready, let’s kick off.”

🧭

walk you through

vous guider à travers

Guide the audience step by step.

“Let me walk you through the project story.”

↩

circle back

revenir sur

Return to a point later.

“I’ll circle back to that during the Q&A.”

✓

recap

récapituler

Summarise the main message.

“Let me quickly recap the three key points.”

?

clarify

clarifier

Make sure you understand the question.

“Can I clarify what you mean by lead time?”

⚠️

not overclaim

ne pas trop affirmer

Avoid saying more than the slide proves.

“The slide shows the target, but not the final root cause yet.”

🔎

causes / facteurs sous-jacents

The real reasons behind the delay.

“The next step is to identify the underlying drivers.”

👋

How’s it going?

Comment ça va ?

A natural greeting.

“Hey, how’s it going?”

💬

What have you been up to?

Quoi de neuf ?

Ask what someone has been doing recently.

“What have you been up to outside work?”

06 · GRAMMAR FOR THE KICKOFF

Use grammar to show time, cause and caution.

These structures will help you sound precise without sounding too technical.

CURRENT SITUATIONPresent simple

“The process takes too long today.”

GOALTarget language

“The target is to reduce the P90 lead time to 2 days.”

POSSIBLE IMPACTCan / could

“This can affect delivery commitments.”

CAUTIONAt this stage

“At this stage, the slide shows the target, not the root cause.”

Choose the best grammar for the meeting

1. Today, the process ___ too long.

2. The target is ___ the P90 lead time to 2 days.

3. Long lead time ___ customer commitments.

4. The slide shows the target, but it ___ the final root cause.

5. During the analyze phase, we ___ the underlying drivers.

6. ___, delivery risk should decrease.

07 · QUESTIONS WITHOUT OVERCLAIMING

Invite questions, but protect accuracy.

The strongest answer is not always the fastest answer. It is the answer that is clear, honest and supported by the slide.

1

Acknowledge

“That’s a good question.”

→
2

Clarify

“When you say lead time, do you mean P90?”

→
3

Answer

One clear point.

→
4

Evidence

Use the slide only if it proves the point.

→
5

Next step

“We’ll confirm that in the analyze phase.”

Choose the safest professional answer

1. “Why exactly is the process taking 12 days?”

2. “Is 2 days realistic?”

3. “What exactly is in scope?”

4. “What is the biggest risk?”

ONLY AFTER THE COACHING ABOVE

Press “New question” when you are ready.

Now connect the pieces without reading the slide.

Use the slide as a visual support. You are the story.

0:45–1:45

2 · Problem + target

1:45–2:45

Full supported model · B1/B1+

“Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here. I’m here to present a Kaizen project led by a cross-functional team. The project is about non-conformity treatment, or NNC. The simple story is that today, the P90 lead time is 12 days, and the target is 2 days.

This matters because long processing time can affect on-time delivery, respect of commitments, customer satisfaction and parts holding costs. So the project is not only about one internal metric. It is about protecting the customer promise and making the process easier to control.

The scope is focused. We are looking at turbine nozzles and blades for CFM56 and LEAP. GE engineering analysis cases are out of scope, so the team can concentrate on the cases where action is possible within this Kaizen project.

The roadmap follows DMAIC: define, measure and analyze, improve, then control. The control phase is important because the objective is not a temporary improvement. The objective is to make the improvement sustainable.

That is the main story: reduce the lead time from 12 days to 2 days, focus on the right scope and use the roadmap to make the improvement last. I’m happy to take your questions.”

Stronger model · B2

“Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining this kickoff. I’ll keep the story simple. The project is about reducing the lead time for non-conformity treatment in the turbine area. Today, the P90 lead time is 12 days, or 288 hours. Our target is 2 days, or 48 hours.

The reason this matters is straightforward. Long treatment time creates pressure on delivery commitments, customer satisfaction and parts holding costs. So the metric is not just an internal indicator; it has a real operational and financial impact.

The project scope is deliberately focused. We are looking at turbine nozzles and blades for CFM56 and LEAP, while GE engineering analysis cases are outside the scope. That focus should help the team move from diagnosis to action more effectively.

The roadmap is structured around DMAIC: define, measure and analyze, improve, then control at 30, 60 and 90 days. That last point is important: the goal is not simply to improve once, but to control the process so the improvement is sustainable.

So the key message is this: we have a clear problem, a measurable target, a focused scope and a roadmap for control. I’ll pause here and take your questions.”
